cf.title: Add an ETW backend for the static probes on Windows

input.subject: [PATCH] Add an ETW backend for the static probes on Windows

verdict_reasoning: No surviving objection is fatal, and the goal follows existing practice: the same probes already have DTrace and SystemTap backends. The remaining points are fixable design questions. They are the default-on exposure of query text (security-1), the UTF-8 tag on strings sent in the server encoding (standards-compat-2), the second probe file (maintenance-fit-1) and the unstated schema stability rule (standards-compat-1). Demand evidence is thin (demand-1), but parity is a fair reason to keep reading.

brief.title: ETW backend for the static probes on Windows
brief.problem: Windows builds use the dummy probes.h, so the static probes are compiled out and cannot be traced there. DTrace and SystemTap cover other platforms, but Postgres has no backend for Event Tracing for Windows (ETW).
brief.proposed_design: The probe macros expand to TraceLogging events from one provider, "PostgreSQL.Server", registered once per process and removed at process exit. A new data file, probes_etw.txt, gives each probe a keyword, a level and argument names. probes.d stays the source of truth, and the build fails on every platform if the two files disagree.
user_visible_surface: New meson option -Detw (auto, enabled, disabled), default auto, mutually exclusive with -Ddtrace; MinGW builds keep the dummy probes.
ETW provider "PostgreSQL.Server" with GUID ea7811de-e757-5488-7ad6-2b057cced37d, documented as a stable contract that never changes.
Event names match the DTrace probe names with underscores, and fields are named, with keywords such as QUERY, LOCK and BUFFER and levels INFO or VERBOSE.
New file src/backend/utils/probes_etw.txt, which every new probe needs, plus a build check on all platforms.
String arguments are tagged UTF-8 but passed in the server encoding, and are clipped to 32kB.
author_claims: No new probes and no change to probes.d or the call sites; only the macro expansion changes.
On pgbench -S, an idle ETW build was within 0.5% of the dummy build, which the author calls noise.
Probe arguments are evaluated only when a session has enabled the event.
Events show up in wpr and WPA in the same trace as kernel disk and scheduler events.
brief.thread_state: Only the first message is visible, and no one has replied. The CommitFest entry is in Needs review for version 20.
unclear: The material does not give the overhead with a trace session active, for example with VERBOSE lwlock or buffer events enabled.
The patch does not say how consumers decode non-UTF-8 strings tagged as UTF-8, or what happens with a cut multibyte character.
The material does not say whether autoconf/make builds can build the ETW backend, or only run the consistency check.
The material does not say who may enable the provider, or whether query text in events raises security or privacy concerns.
Registering once per process touches postmaster.c and miscinit.c, but the material does not say how EXEC_BACKEND children register.

objections.title: Default-on ETW exposes all sessions' query text to Performance Log Users
objections.failure_scenario: A packager ships an MSVC build, where -Detw=auto turns the provider on. An operator who is in Performance Log Users, but not an administrator and not the service account, runs the logman command from message #1. The .etl file then holds every backend's query text, including literals and `alter role ... password` statements, and no one in Postgres can see that this happened.
objections.argument: On other platforms the probes are off unless the build uses --enable-dtrace, and tracing them needs root or similar rights. This patch turns the probes on by default in MSVC builds. Message #1 says capture needs only Performance Log Users membership, a group meant for delegated monitoring. The query, query__parse and statement__status probes carry text that log_statement keeps under superuser control. The docs hunks give no security note and do not say who may enable the provider.
objections.author_must_show: Why is it acceptable for Performance Log Users members to read every session's query text by default, and should the QUERY strings or the default be gated?

critic.reasoning: Message #1 says membership in Performance Log Users is enough to capture, and the QUERY events carry full query text. The visible docs give no security note, and the default is auto.

objections.title: Strings tagged as UTF-8 but sent in the server encoding
objections.failure_scenario: A DBA traces a cluster whose databases use WIN1252 or EUC_JP and opens the trace in WPA or tracerpt. These tools decode query text as UTF-8, so non-ASCII characters show as replacement characters or the field fails to decode. A query clipped at 32kB can also end in a partial multibyte character.
objections.argument: The commit message says string arguments are tagged UTF-8 but passed in the server encoding, so the tag is wrong for every non-UTF-8 database. Windows clusters often use legacy code pages, so this affects a real share of the users this backend targets. TraceLogging has field types for ANSI strings and counted binary data that would not make a false encoding claim. The proposal does not say how a consumer should decode these fields.
objections.author_must_show: How does a WPA or tracerpt user get correct query text from a WIN1252 or EUC database, and how is a cut multibyte character handled?

critic.reasoning: The commit message itself says strings are tagged UTF-8 but passed in the server encoding and clipped at 32kB. The material does not show how common legacy encodings are on Windows, but the wrong tag stands for any non-UTF-8 database.

objections.title: Every probe change on every platform must now edit probes_etw.txt
objections.failure_scenario: A Linux developer adds an argument to an lwlock probe in probes.d. The build fails on their machine until they also edit probes_etw.txt and choose an ETW keyword, level and field name for a facility they never use. Argument descriptions now live in probes.d, monitoring.sgml and probes_etw.txt.
objections.argument: The commit message makes the consistency check run in meson and make builds without ETW, so the cost falls on all developers while only MSVC Windows users gain (item 4). The check fails loudly, which answers item 9, but it adds a third copy of each argument's type, plus a field name that the file header says is copied by hand from monitoring.sgml. A committer would likely ask whether keyword, level and names could be derived or defaulted, so that probes.d stays the only file to edit.
objections.author_must_show: Why can probes_etw.txt not be generated, or given defaults, from probes.d and the existing documentation, so a non-Windows probe change needs no second file?

critic.reasoning: The commit message confirms the check runs in builds without ETW, and the file header says field names are copied from monitoring.sgml. The proposal does not say why keyword, level and names cannot be defaulted.

objections.title: Keyword bits and event fields become a contract with no stated stability rule
objections.failure_scenario: An admin saves a logman or wpr profile that filters on keyword mask 0x3 and level 4, as message #1 shows. A later release reorders the PG_KW_* bits or renames a probe argument in probes_etw.txt. The saved profile then captures the wrong events or fields, and the admin finds out only when a trace comes back empty or mislabeled.
objections.argument: The docs promise that the provider name and GUID never change. Capture profiles also depend on the keyword bit values, the levels, the event names and the field names, and the example in message #1 hard-codes the mask 0x3. The proposal does not say whether these stay stable across major versions or may change with probes.d. Without a stated rule, users will treat them as stable, and every later probe change becomes a compatibility question.
objections.author_must_show: Which parts of the event schema (keyword bits, levels, event and field names) are promised stable across major versions, and how are users told when they change?

critic.reasoning: The visible docs promise stability only for the provider name and GUID. The example in message #1 hard-codes the keyword mask 0x3, so saved profiles depend on bits and names that have no stated rule.

objections.title: No evidence that Windows users want to trace the static probes
objections.failure_scenario: The project adds and documents a provider GUID as a contract that "never changes", plus a second probe file that has to be kept up to date. If few Windows users ever start an ETW session for it, the project keeps that contract and file for years for a feature with little use.
objections.argument: Message #1 gives parity with other platforms as the only reason. It cites no field report, no -general or -bugs thread, no second user and no production story. Even on Linux and macOS the static probes need a build option that is off by default, so their user base may be small already. No one has replied in the thread.
objections.author_must_show: Which Windows users or support cases needed these probes, what did they use instead, and will the common Windows installers ship with -Detw enabled?

critic.reasoning: Message #1 gives platform parity as the only reason and names no user or support case. Parity explains the goal, but it does not show that enough people will use it to justify a permanent GUID contract and a second probe file.

refuted.title: Default auto differs from dtrace, which defaults to disabled
refuted.failure_scenario: A packager rebuilds Windows binaries with the usual meson command and now ships ETW-enabled servers without choosing to. On those servers, any member of Performance Log Users can capture query text from every database. The packager learns this only when a user reports it.
refuted.argument: The -Ddtrace option defaults to disabled, so tracing support is opt-in today. The -Detw option defaults to auto, so it is turned on whenever the SDK header exists. Message #1 reports low idle overhead, but the proposal does not give a reason for departing from the dtrace default, whose consequences also fall on users who never asked for tracing.
refuted.author_must_show: Why should -Detw default to auto when -Ddtrace defaults to disabled, and what do packagers need to know before shipping it on?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of security-1, which states the same default-on consequence with a concrete scenario. The consistency part is weak, because the gssapi option in the same meson_options.txt hunk also defaults to auto.

refuted.title: Default auto differs from dtrace, which defaults to disabled
refuted.failure_scenario: Windows packagers who build with MSVC get the ETW backend without asking, so every enabled probe site in lwlock and buffer code becomes a live check in shipped binaries. A regression on a workload other than pgbench -S shows up only after users report it.
refuted.argument: meson_options.txt keeps dtrace at 'disabled' but sets etw to 'auto', and the proposal gives no reason for the difference. The only measurement is one idle pgbench -S run within 0.5%, which the author calls noise. That run does not show the cost of the enabled-check at high-volume VERBOSE sites under contention. A committer would likely ask for the same default as dtrace, or for measurements that justify shipping the backend on by default.
refuted.author_must_show: Which measurements on lwlock-heavy and buffer-heavy workloads justify an auto default for ETW when dtrace defaults to disabled?

critic.reasoning: The objection names no workload that would regress, and pgbench -S already passes through the lwlock and buffer probe sites with the provider idle. The cost with a session active falls only on users who trace. The default question is covered by security-1.

refuted.title: Windows-only backend with no engaged committer to maintain it
refuted.failure_scenario: A later Windows SDK changes TraceLogging macro behaviour, or a new probe argument type does not map to a TraceLogging field type. The Visual Studio CI task breaks. The committer who sees the failure cannot test locally and must wait for one of the few Windows-qualified committers.
refuted.argument: The backend depends on a Windows SDK header of a version "recent enough", which is an external part the project does not control (item 15). It adds per-process registration in postmaster.c and miscinit.c. Only message #1 exists, and no committer has replied. Coverage depends on one CI task that has to opt in explicitly, because the CI sets auto_features to disabled.
refuted.author_must_show: Which committer familiar with the Windows build has agreed to own this backend, and what minimum SDK version will be supported?

critic.reasoning: A thread with no reply after two weeks fits any new Windows patch, and the rubric puts ownership under committability, separate from the design verdict. The SDK breakage scenario is speculative, since the proposal does not show that TraceLogging macros change behaviour.

refuted.title: Every probe author pays for probes_etw.txt, on every platform
refuted.failure_scenario: A developer on Linux adds or changes a probe in probes.d. The build fails until they also pick an ETW keyword, a level and field names in probes_etw.txt, for a backend they cannot build or test.
refuted.argument: The commit message says make and meson builds without ETW still run the consistency check. So the cost falls on everyone who touches probes.d, while only Windows MSVC users who trace get any benefit. The design choice is a fair way to stop silent mislabeling, but it moves Windows upkeep onto all platforms. It is easier to accept if the demand case above is made.
refuted.author_must_show: Could the ETW metadata be generated from probes.d with defaults, so that only Windows builds fail when a probe has no ETW entry?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of maintenance-fit-1, which makes the same point about probes_etw.txt in more detail.

touch_points.label: ABI / extension API
touch_points.reason: The probe macros in probes.h now expand to TraceLogging calls on a provider handle, which Windows extensions that use the macros would need.

touch_points.label: security / privileges
touch_points.reason: QUERY events carry query text, and message #1 says membership in Performance Log Users is enough to capture them.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: see objection standards-compat-1: Keyword bits and event fields become a contract with no stated stability rule

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: The patch adds probes_etw.txt, a build check on every platform, a permanent provider GUID and a dependency on a Windows SDK header.

touch_points.label: performance on the hot path
touch_points.reason: Probe sites in lwlock and buffer code become live enabled-checks in default MSVC builds.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)
touch_points.reason: see objection demand-1: No evidence that Windows users want to trace the static probes

questions: Who may enable the provider, and should the query text fields or the auto default be gated, given that Performance Log Users members can capture every session's queries?
How does a WPA or tracerpt user read query text from a WIN1252 or EUC_JP database, and what happens to a multibyte character cut at 32kB?
Can the keyword, level and field names be generated or defaulted from probes.d, so that a probe change on a non-Windows platform needs no edit to probes_etw.txt?
Which parts of the event schema (keyword bits, levels, event names, field names) stay stable across major versions, besides the provider name and GUID?
Which Windows users or support cases needed these probes, and what did they use instead?

committability.owner_note: It needs a committer who knows the Windows MSVC build and process startup under EXEC_BACKEND, and who can test with wpr or logman.
committability.liability: The owner signs for a provider name and GUID documented as never changing, an event schema users will save in capture profiles, a dependency on a Windows SDK header, and a build check that every later probe change must pass.
committability.author_follow_up: No sign either way; only message #1 exists. The patch set includes a CI change and docs.

priority.reason: The benefit goes to Windows MSVC users who trace, and the main patch is about 32 KiB across the build system, postmaster.c and miscinit.c. The security default and the string encoding should be settled before code review, since both change what the provider emits.

provisional_note: Without the code, three things could not be checked: how EXEC_BACKEND children register the provider, whether Windows extensions that use the probe macros can link to it, and the overhead with VERBOSE lock and buffer events enabled.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: pg_tracing
precedents_retrieved.summary: A contrib-style extension, pg_tracing, generates distributed-tracing spans for planner, executor and nested queries, using trace context passed in SQLCommenter comments or a sampling rate. Spans go into a shared memory buffer, and an external forwarder reads them with pg_tracing_consume_spans() and sends them to a trace collector.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Heikki Linnakangas recommended that the author publish pg_tracing as a separate extension on GitHub, and Nikita Malakhov agreed. Heikki's own message is not shown; only the replies quote it. In March 2024 the author said he was moving pg_tracing to a GitHub repository, and the entry was later withdrawn. The visible messages do not show a technical objection that blocked the patch.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: To give a quick update: following Heikki's suggestion, I'm currently working on getting pg_tracing as a separate extension on github.

precedents_retrieved.title: Report tranche ID and LWLock pointer in LWLock static tracepoints
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch set adds the LWLock pointer and the numeric tranche ID to each LWLock static tracepoint, so traces can tell individual locks apart and compare them across processes. It also fixes misplaced tracepoints, adds a single tracepoint for all acquires and releases plus start markers for timing, and adds comments on LWLock tranches.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Two parts were committed by Peter Eisentraut: the removal of the wrong lwlock__acquire tracepoint in LWLockWaitForVar, and the move of TRACE_POSTGRESQL_LWLOCK_RELEASE. In his last review he reported that patch 0002 did not build on macOS because uint64 was used in the probe definitions, and that the probe changes had no documentation. He also asked for a different argument order and whether both tranche name and tranche ID are needed. The visible messages show no new version after that review.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
First, a problem:  0002 doesn't build on macOS, because uint64 has been
used in the probe definitions.

precedents_retrieved.title: libpq trace log
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch began as a libpq client-side query log enabled by connection parameters or environment variables (logdir/PGLOGDIR, logsize/PGLOGSIZE). After review it was narrowed to reworking PQtrace() so it prints one line per protocol message with a timestamp, and enabling it without recompiling was deferred.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Earlier, David Steele moved the patch to PG13 because, in agreement with Andres, it was not clear where the patch was going. The last message before the decision is a review by Alvaro Herrera, who agreed with the one-line-per-message direction but asked for changes. He objected to a frontend_entry[MAXPGPATH] array in pg_conn and listed smaller fixes. The thread shows no new patch or author reply after that review before the entry was returned.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: This seems to make pg_conn much larger than we'd like.

precedents_retrieved.title: Windows meson build
precedents_retrieved.summary: The first patch set added Windows-specific meson code to find icu, libxml, libxslt, lz4, tcl, zlib and zstd without pkgconf. After objections, the patch became a documentation change that describes PKG_CONFIG_PATH, vcpkg, and the -Dextra_include_dirs and -Dextra_lib_dirs options.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Peter Eisentraut and Andres Freund rejected the code patches because they added a separate Windows path for finding dependencies, and they asked the author to use pkgconf or cmake. Peter Eisentraut later returned the documentation patch, saying it covered only one scenario that worked for the author and moved text out of context. He suggested a how-to document or blog post instead.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
In any case, I don't think your patch has
enough coverage to make this better, it just describes some specific
scenario that works for you, and it moves some text out of context where
it doesn't make sense anymore.

precedents_retrieved.title: Implement <null treatment> for window functions
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds the SQL-standard RESPECT NULLS and IGNORE NULLS syntax to all true window functions, without hardcoding the standard's list of functions, and adds TREAT NULLS to CREATE FUNCTION. It does not implement FROM LAST.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The patch failed to compile under GCC with -Werror because 'step' may be used uninitialized in WinGetFuncArgInPartition and WinGetFuncArgInFrame. No new version came in for two months, so Michael Paquier marked it returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
This was two months ago, so this patch has been marked as returned
with feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: Fix severe performance regression with gettext 0.20+ on Windows
precedents_retrieved.summary: On Windows with gettext 0.20 and later, the patch sets LC_MESSAGES in Windows locale format ("English_United States.1252") instead of converting it with IsoLocaleName(). This avoids a gettext bug where failed locale lookups were not cached, so every gettext() call enumerated all system locales and exception-heavy workloads ran about 5 times slower.
precedents_retrieved.objection: gettext 1.0 fixed the upstream caching bug, which made the workaround unnecessary. Peter Eisentraut found gettext 1.0 alone about 10 times faster, and the patch on top of it about 25% slower. The author traced this to an uncached Windows-format path in gettext and concluded the patch is not needed for gettext 1.0 and later.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
But when I apply your patch, it actually makes things worse (by about
25%).

precedents_retrieved.title: Fix Windows network event handling
precedents_retrieved.summary: On Windows, the patch moves socket event handles out of each WaitEventSet into a reference-counted per-socket hash table, and adds its own level-triggered event memory, so the edge-triggered FD_CLOSE event is no longer lost. It also changes simplehash for raw malloc/free and no-OOM behaviour, and would let the graceful socket shutdown on Windows be put back.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The entry was returned with feedback in the 2024-01 commitfest because CFbot showed test failures and no updated version followed. In review, Robert Haas questioned the simplehash changes: whether SH_RAW_FREE is needed, whether the no-OOM change in 0002 is a good idea at all, and why raw malloc/free is used instead of palloc/pfree. The visible messages show no reply to that review.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I wonder whether we really want 0002. It seems like a pretty significant behavior change -- now everybody using simplehash has to worry about whether failure cases are possible.

precedents_retrieved.title: CREATE COLLATION default provider
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch changes CREATE COLLATION so that the provider defaults to libc when LC_COLLATE or LC_CTYPE is given, and otherwise to the provider of the current database's default collation. The provider chosen at initdb would then carry through CREATE DATABASE to CREATE COLLATION.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Peter Eisentraut doubted the practical use, because the user usually must know the provider to spell the locale name, and common locales are already preloaded. He also objected that the default should come only top-down from datlocprovider, not also from the other CREATE COLLATION options. Earlier, the author himself doubted that datlocprovider is a good signal and suggested a GUC instead. He agreed with both points and withdrew the patch.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Also, I think the default should only flow one way, top-down:  The
default provider of CREATE COLLATION is datlocprovider.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found. [P3] adds arguments to the LWLock tracepoints and stalled on a macOS build failure and missing docs, which does not apply to a Windows backend. [P6] and [P8] are DTrace reverts with no recorded reason, and message #1 cites no earlier discussion of ETW.
Objections are listed above. The idea of an ETW backend fits existing practice, and none of these objections is fatal.

The proposal has no persistent or cross-node state: no on-disk format, WAL, catalog, replication or wire protocol change, and probes.d and its call sites stay the same. Without the code I could not check two things: whether extensions built on Windows that call TRACE_POSTGRESQL_* macros can link to the provider handle, and how EXEC_BACKEND children register.

One objection on exposure. Not evaluated without the code: whether an unprivileged OS user can slow the server by enabling the VERBOSE lock and buffer events, because the material gives no overhead figure for an active trace session.
Not applicable; three fixable objections raised.

No existing feature gives this result on Windows: the probes compile to the dummy probes.h there, and no extension or hook can supply them, since the macro expansion happens at compile time. The patch extends the existing probes.d mechanism rather than adding a second one, and I am not sure enough about any external Windows tool that reads these static probes to name it.
Both objections point to missing demand evidence, not to a flaw in the idea. Measured overhead with a trace session active, and security, are left to other angles.

warnings: synthesis said NEEDS-COMMITTER-EYES but listed a level 1b objection (demand-1); changed to NEEDS-DESIGN-DISCUSSION
